drills.title: Name That Toxidrome
drills.description: Fast pattern recognition. Read the signs, pick the agent or the antidote. Wrong answer = wrong drug.

items.prompt: Pinpoint pupils, drooling, wheezing, twitching, vomiting.
Pinpoint pupils, RR 4, dry skin, no twitching, crowd in a theater.
items.why: Dry miosis + respiratory depression = opioid → naloxone.

items.prompt: Fire victim, unresponsive, BP 70/40, SpO2 reads 99%.
items.why: Smoke + shock → cyanide (and CO). Hydroxocobalamin is the antidote.

items.prompt: Yellow-green cloud, bleach smell, immediate burning eyes and stridor.
'Smelled like cut hay', mild cough now; feels fine.
items.why: Phosgene: delayed pulmonary edema 2–24 h. Rest and observe.

items.prompt: Painless garlic-smelling oily liquid; red blistering skin appears 6 h later.
items.why: Mustard: painless exposure, delayed blisters. Decon immediately — no antidote.

items.prompt: Immediate severe skin pain, geranium odor, blistering.
items.why: Lewisite hurts immediately; antidote is BAL (dimercaprol).

items.prompt: Protesters: tearing, burning skin, coughing; improving after 20 min in fresh air.
items.why: CS/OC effects are immediate and self-limited after removal.
Severe = 3 kits rapidly + benzo + ventilatory support.

items.prompt: Atropine has been given. Pulse 128, pupils still tiny, chest now clear and breathing easy. Next?
options: Stop — endpoint reached (dry secretions, easy breathing)
items.why: Titrate to secretions/breathing — tachycardia and miosis aren't the endpoint.

items.prompt: Basement, rotten-egg smell that 'disappeared', 3 workers collapsed.
options: Hydrogen sulfide — do not enter; SCBA only
items.why: H2S paralyzes smell at high concentration — a classic multiple-rescuer death scenario.

items.prompt: Farmer after spraying crops: sweating, diarrhea, miosis, bradycardia.
items.why: Organophosphate pesticides = same mechanism as nerve agents.
